nekudot-hakesef.1#_: (siman 119 in Taz s.k. 4) And his words are astounding in this gloss. See in Shach s.k. 6 I settled his words on the matter that they are correct for practical halachah.
nekudot-hakesef.2#_: (there in Shach s.k. 7) And in Bach he explained, etc., and milk and morayis and bread and cheese and the like — that requiring one seal does not deal with except a gentile, but one deposits with a suspected person even without a seal, etc.; so one must say and so in Bach there see there.
nekudot-hakesef.3#_: (there in Taz s.k. 7) Nevertheless there is a difficulty on Beit Yosef who wrote it is known the halachah is like R' Shimon, etc.; Bach already preceded this.
nekudot-hakesef.4#_: (there s.k. 8) Likewise in the Perishah. See Shach s.k. 13 he strained for nothing.
nekudot-hakesef.5#_: (there s.k. 9) Also in this it is wondrous, etc.; one must say as I wrote in Shach s.k. 19.
nekudot-hakesef.6#_: (there s.k. 12) It appears from this that even if the prohibition is safek tereifah, etc. — meaning even safek tereifah which is forbidden only in eating; likewise explicit in his words in notes 13–14; not clear a contradiction that the seller will say it is not kosher and the buyer must bring proof; Rashi deals with a firstborn forbidden in benefit — likewise d'rabbanan forbidden in benefit requires returning money, for benefit-prohibition has no law of sale at all; d'rabbanan prohibition and safek prohibition share one law; further it appears there regarding firstborn it is like not checking the lung which is a rabbinic enactment — likewise showing a firstborn is their enactment as below siman 309; on the contrary showing firstborn is stricter for we find in mishnah and Gemara one must show a sage; if so it is like something forbidden in benefit d'rabbanan; what Rashi wrote safek prohibition means therefore they penalized him because of safek prohibition they touched it — meaning the Sages enacted thus out of doubt; likewise lung checking they enacted out of doubt; know that Rashi's intent is as I explained and this is clear. I again found as my words in Semak Choshen Mishpat siman 234: only for certain tereifah; but for safek tereifah he need not return money if eaten; and a slaughterer who sold a cow and it became known tereifah — he returns even if already eaten — meaning certainly tereifah; and firstborn differs for an animal is presumed without defect; also firstborn not checked — even if afterward known it had a defect — still forbidden in benefit d'rabbanan as mishnah chapter Ad Kamah and Tur Yoreh Deah siman 310; since it is benefit-prohibition the seller does not deduct from payment and the reason is sensible: even if intact the seller would have to discard and not benefit — therefore no law of sale; as above; and clear from his words even if the seller knew before sale it is safek tereifah he need not return if eaten; if he did not know, even certain tereifah they do not penalize as Shach s.k. 25.
nekudot-hakesef.7#_: (there in Taz s.k. 15) He explained even though Shulchan Aruch wrote, etc. This explanation is not so as Shach s.k. 29 and I proved nearby it is not so.
nekudot-hakesef.8#_: (there end s.k. 18) He extended to challenge — meaning even d'oraisa prohibitions the law is so; according to Shach s.k. 37 one must say see there.
